stories.title: 'Will petrol be available in December?': Senate echoes with shortage concerns even as state minister says no supply issues
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Senate echoed with fuel supply concerns on Friday as PPP’s Sherry Rehman questioned petrol availability for December and Opposition Leader Raja Nasir Abbas warned of a bleak situation amid heightening Middle East tensions.

Senator Rehman said reports of renewed attacks on Iran and escalating conflict in West Asia had added to uncertainty surrounding Pakistan’s petroleum supplies and had direct implications for the country’s energy security, economic stability and lives of ordinary citizens.

Finance Minister Aurangzeb said during an interview last week that Pakistan had so far withstood the shock from skyrocketing energy prices, but attacks on infrastructure in Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries were “worrying” for the country’s longer-term economic outlook.

stories.title: NCCIA prevents Karachi girl exposed to dark web group from causing self-harm: official
summary: KARACHI: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) prevented a teenage girl in Karachi from causing self-harm after she was influenced by a group operating on the dark web, an official told Dawn on Friday.
NCCIA Karachi Additional Director Tariq Nawaz said action by the agency was taken after they received a lead from a foreign crime investigation agency, which he did not name.

The NCCIA had received another tip-off from a foreign agency earlier this month in another case involving a teenager, who was sent to jail on judicial remand for allegedly attempting to poison his father after seeking help from artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots.

stories.title: German president meets Zardari, praises Pakistan's 'rising diplomatic profile' in dispute resolution
summary: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier praised Pakistan’s “rising diplomatic profile in the resolution of regional and global disputes”, in a meeting with President Asif Ali Zardari in Berlin on Friday.
President Zardari further expressed his gratitude for Steinmeier’s acknowledgement of Pakistan’s “sincere mediation role” in the conflict between the United States and Iran, the statement said.
In a statement issued on Thursday, the Foreign Office (FO) said the president’s visit, scheduled for Oct 22-24, is “part of high-level exchanges between Pakistan and Germany”.

stories.title: R4 bloc, European powers discuss developments in the Gulf in Istanbul meeting
summary: Developments in the Gulf region amid the US-Israeli war on Iran came under discussion as the R4 foreign ministers — Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye — met with their counterparts from France, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom.

According to the FO, Dar participated in the sixth R4 foreign ministers’ meeting alongside Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, and Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud of Saudi Arabia.

Separately, DPM Dar met with German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul on the sidelines of the meeting and expressed the desire to further strengthen bilateral ties “through sustained engagement and cooperation across multiple areas of mutual interest”, the FO said.

stories.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia have completed ratification of Makkah defence pact: FO
summary: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have completed the ratification processes for the Makkah defence pact while Turkiye was in the process of doing so, Foreign Office (FO) spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan said on Friday.
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in August, under which an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.

Earlier this month, the FO said that Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye had agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom, following an emergency meeting of the SPDC formed under their joint defence agreement in Riyadh.

stories.title: Trump says another op against Iran on cards
summary: US President Donald Trump said on Friday Washington may carry out another military operation against Iran at a time when the war is nearing its eight month mark and as rise in fuel prices weigh on the US midterm elections.
"We may do another little Epic Fury," Trump said in remarks at a rally in Florida as he spoke about the war.
"Operation Epic Fury" is the name used by the US military for its war against Iran.

stories.title: CDF Munir vows to hit terror outfits hard
summary: Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir vowed to continue the campaign against "Indian-sponsored terrorist outfits" and "hit them hard wherever they are", the military's media wing said on Friday.

In Balochistan, security forces killed 10 terrorists, including a woman, during operations in Gwadar after Indian-sponsored Fitna al-Hindustan terrorists attempted attacks near the Gabd border crossing and in Gwadar city, the military's media wing said on Friday.
"Security forces foiled the terrorists' designs and their bid to undermine the writ of the state and spread their misconstrued agenda," the statement said.

stories.title: PM sets wheat support price at Rs4,500
summary: Separately, National Food Security Minister Rana Tanveer Hussain has promised a better support price for wheat farmers this season, saying Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif will coordinate with the provinces to establish a uniform rate as the government seeks to stabilise the market.
Noting that Pakistan possessed vast potential in the livestock sector, the prime minister stressed that it should be harnessed for exports and economic growth.

Alvarez & Marsal Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reiterated Pakistan's willingness to open its economy to promising international markets and consult globally recognised economic experts to advance the country's economic growth and prosperity.

stories.title: Regional powers back Islamabad MoU
summary: Pakistan, Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Egypt on Friday threw their collective weight behind the Islamabad-brokered understanding between Iran and the United States, as regional and European powers stepped up diplomatic efforts to prevent another round of hostilities in the Gulf.
Dar briefed his counterparts on Islamabad's mediation efforts during the subsequent expanded meeting with European foreign ministers.
The urgency surrounding the meeting was underscored by Turkish Foreign Minister Fidan, who warned after the talks that renewed military action against Iran would only deepen instability.

stories.title: Twelve killed in Lasbela road accident
summary: At least twelve people were killed and around two dozen sustained injuries when a passenger van smashed into a passenger bus on Friday in Lasbela district of Balochistan.

Soon after the collision, police, rescue officials, district administration, and local people started rescue work, removing the dead and the injured from the mangled vehicles and shifting them to a hospital in Lasbela.
Talking to the media, Lasbela's Edhi Centre In-charge Dr Abdul Hakeem Lasi said seven people died on the spot as a result of the crash while five succumbed to their injuries in the hospital.

stories.title: Fuel fears dominate Senate as winter looms
summary: Concerns over Pakistan's petroleum supplies amid escalating tensions in the Middle East dominated the Senate proceedings on Friday, with lawmakers demanding clarity on the government's contingency plans even as the finance minister maintained that there was no fuel shortage.

Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Senator Sherry Rehman questioned whether the country would have sufficient petroleum supplies in December and urged the government to brief parliament on its contingency and possible rationing plans.

Rehman also questioned the utilisation of the carbon levy imposed on petroleum products, alleging that the proceeds were being absorbed into general federal revenues rather than spent on environmental protection and climate resilience projects.

stories.title: US First Lady secures truce for Ukraine city
summary: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a temporary ceasefire in the Russian-controlled southern Ukrainian city of Oleshky to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and civilian evacuations, following mediation by US First Lady Melania Trump, the White House said on Friday.
The ceasefire will enable humanitarian teams to enter the city, where residents have reported a worsening food crisis.
He said the agreement followed an extended process involving Melania Trump and Pope Leo and would establish a humanitarian corridor for residents seeking to leave the city.

stories.title: Turkey says Libya will unify soon
summary: Turkey backed the UN-recognised government in Tripoli, but ties with authorities in eastern Libya have warmed significantly in recent years.
On Tuesday, Libya's eastern-based parliament approved a maritime demarcation deal with Turkey.
These structures need to be brought together under a national army," he added.

stories.title: Mohmand Dam cost jumps 115%
summary: The revised project cost was presented before the Central Development Working Party (CDWP) meeting this week, which did not take up the matter for a decision due to paucity of time, according to federal government officials.

It was explained that the project contains both local and foreign currency components and that fluctuations in the dollar exchange rate have resulted in a significant increase in the rupee equivalent of the foreign component.
The Planning Commission had asked Wapda to provide details of dollar-denominated contractual payments and the extent to which exchange-rate variation could be passed on to the project cost.

stories.title: Unnecessary rules being removed
summary: Adviser to Prime Minister for Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan has said that the government is undertaking reforms to simplify business environment, remove unnecessary regulatory hurdles and promote domestic and foreign investment in Pakistan.

Addressing a press conference alongside Gilgit-Baltistan chief minister and members of his cabinet, the adviser said that complexity of the regulatory framework and difficulties in doing business had been among the major factors discouraging foreign investment in Pakistan.
The proposed amendments will facilitate company registrations and business operations while modernising Pakistan's corporate regulatory framework.

stories.title: Small factories choose to stay small
summary: Small-scale manufacturers are increasingly squeezed by rising raw material, scrap, transport and energy costs, leaving them with slimmer profits per unit.

Across the industrial areas of Sher Shah, SITE, Korangi, Landhi, Federal B Area and SITE Super Highway, small manufacturers producing essential packaging and high-demand domestic plastic goods are making a deliberate choice to remain small.
"The consumer market for basic plastic items such as plates, bowls, jugs and storage containers is huge," explains Mohammad Nadeem, a small-scale plastic moulding and recycling operator.

stories.title: Bangladesh trade 'several billion' short of potential
summary: Speaking at the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry, he identified agriculture, textiles, pharmaceuticals, engineering, food processing, chemicals, minerals, education, healthcare and tourism as promising areas of collaboration, according to a statement on Friday.
Bangladeshi pineapples had begun reaching Pakistan after clearances, and seasonal fruits, agricultural products and jaggery could further expand trade.

He called for easier business visas, improved e-visa procedures and stronger direct air connectivity, noting Pakistan could serve as a gateway to Central Asia while Bangladesh offered access to Southeast Asia.

stories.title: Lahore DC gives formal go-ahead for 3-day Basant festivities in March 2027, outlines conditions and restrictions
summary: LAHORE: The Lahore deputy commissioner (DC) on Friday gave the formal go-ahead for three-day Basant festivities in the district from March 12-14 next year, outlining guidelines, conditions and restrictions for the celebrations.
Basant returned to Lahore earlier this year after an 18-year hiatus, with the passing of the Punjab Regulation of Kite Flying Bill, 2025 by the provincial assembly on December 24, 2025.
The notification said the manufacturing of permissible kite-flying material would be allowed from Sept 5, 2026 to March 14, 2027, subject to valid digital registration.

stories.title: Punjab govt to pursue alleged gang-rape case after Azerbaijani victim changes stance
summary: In a recent rape case, it was revealed that the accused’s wealthy family allegedly offered 1.5–2 crore to the victim in exchange for withdrawing her allegations, despite her statement already having been recorded under Section 164.

Lahore Deputy Inspector General (Investigation) Syed Zeeshan Raza said the woman had named three suspects in her judicial statement and that two arrested suspects had also acknowledged the alleged involvement of the third suspect.
He said the video statement appeared to be an attempt to influence the investigation, adding that the third suspect would be included in the investigation and the case would be completed on merit.

stories.title: Rising flour prices fuel weekly inflation
summary: ISLAMABAD: Short-term inflation rose to 11.85 per cent year-on-year in the week ending October 22, driven largely by wheat flour prices, according to official data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) on Friday.

The items whose prices declined week-on-week included tomatoes (21.99pc), petrol (3.63pc), banana (2.42pc), diesel (1.68pc), potatoes (1.38pc), pulse gram (0.93pc), eggs (0.58pc), powdered milk (0.38pc) and broken rice basmati and sugar (0.35pc each).
Last week, short-term inflation rose to 11.38 per cent year-on-year, driven largely by higher food prices, data from PBS showed.

stories.title: UK tells public to keep 3 days' emergency supplies at home following PHP software glitch
summary: The British government advised the public on Friday to keep three days of emergency supplies at home, a message it said had been hammered home by this week’s PHP software glitch, as well as a record-setting summer of heat, drought and wildfires.

The British government said the internet outage showed the importance of its newly launched “Be Ready” campaign, which advises the public to keep three days of bottled water and non-perishable food in the house.
Britain’s advice is similar to that issued by the European Commission, which told EU citizens last year to keep a 72-hour emergency kit containing supplies such as food, water, cash and power banks.

stories.title: Hina Javed’s autopsy reveals brutal torture
summary: According to police sources, the investigation into Hina's murder was not limited to her husband and domestic worker, and inquiries were being conducted from various angles.
Police were also examining whether domestic worker Arshad killed Hina after she allegedly saw him stealing money or other items from the house.
On October 10, a high-level investigation team launched a fresh probe into Hina's murder, visiting the crime scene in Lalkurti and reviewing key evidence, including the victim's DNA report.

stories.title: An uneasy peace
summary: President Trump's wish list for a deal with Iran - under which the Islamic Republic would give up its enriched uranium and provide safe passage for the superpower to exit the volatile region - remains unrealised.
Iran remains adamant that the US must exit the region, as the latter stands badly bruised by the losses it incurred in the war.
American military assets stand depleted in the Middle East, with many key military bases heavily degraded by recent conflict.

stories.title: Organ trade crackdown
summary: Forged referral letters and false donor identities were reportedly used to obtain laboratory tests, while transplants were performed inside residential properties without the necessary medical safeguards.
Hospitals found to have knowingly facilitated illegal procedures must face serious consequences, while medical professionals involved in the trade should be subjected to criminal prosecution.
Enforcement must therefore be accompanied by stronger donor protections and improvements in access to lawful transplantation services.

stories.title: Protecting the watchdogs
summary: The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) regularly ranks Pakistan among the deadliest countries for reporters, with dozens killed in the past two decades, but barely any prosecutions or convictions to show.
CPJ's impunity index has repeatedly highlighted Pakistan's failure to bring the killers of journalists to justice.
The police must treat attacks on journalists as attacks on democratic accountability, with transparent investigations and witness protection.

stories.title: Vishwa Guru's game
summary: By harvesting Israel's weapons-grade Islamophobia and the West's Sinophobia, India manufactured the blind spot for its domestic, regional and eventually global ambitions.
The final phase of the Vishwa Guru project is reshaping the global order in India's image.
By subsuming Islamabad into an Indian civilisational sphere on state television, New Delhi unveiled its own corollary to the Monroe Doctrine or the One China policy.

stories.title: 'NAZA' and a world in disorder
summary: The 48-member Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC), comprising tribal elders from 12 districts for looking after the ex-FATA regions, recalls a proposal discussed in the 1990s to replace the existing FATA administrative arrangement with a tribal advisory council.
Critics also fear that a council dominated by status-quo figures could facilitate a return to the old FATA system in practice, even if the formal structures of provincial government remain in place.
Will it improve coordination among civilian authorities, security agencies and local communities or will the council create another administrative layer without resolving the underlying problems?

stories.title: The only thing moving fast in Karachi is my blood pressure
summary: At this point, Karachi does not need a traffic police department.
I just ask, "How many head injuries away is it?" The person who invented speed breakers in Karachi deserves an award for "Most Creative Way to Torture the General Public Without Going to Jail".
Karachi traffic has its own rules and, apparently, nobody has read them.

stories.title: Sindh reports two more monkeypox cases, tally rises to 98
summary: The Sindh Health Department on Friday reported two more cases of monkeypox, or mpox, taking the provincial tally to 98, as the department stepped up surveillance, contact tracing and patient care following seven new infections in the past week.

Read: Tally hits 95 as two more mpox cases reported in Sindh Citizens have also been advised to maintain proper hand hygiene and avoid direct contact with rashes, blisters and sores on suspected or confirmed patients.
Authorities have consequently emphasised early testing, isolation of confirmed patients, monitoring of close contacts and strict infection-prevention measures in healthcare facilities.

stories.title: NCCIA rescues 13-year-old Karachi girl in probe into suspected dark web network
summary: What began as an online interaction allegedly drew a 13-year-old girl into the orbit of a suspected dark web network, where children were reportedly assigned tasks and paid to produce pornographic animated content.

The agency rescued the girl during a crackdown in Karachi's Rabia City, uncovering what investigators suspect is a wider network involving child exploitation and the production of pornographic cartoons.

Read: NCCIA arrests 4 suspects over child sexual abuse material trafficking in Islamabad Speaking at a press conference, NCCIA Deputy Director Shehzad Akbar said the agency had acted on credible information about the suspected network.

stories.title: Republican 'Muslim Brotherhood' attacks on Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan seek to exploit Democratic fault lines
summary: Rogers has ​sought to undermine the Democrat’s support among Jewish voters by pointing to El-Sayed’s criticism of Israel’s offensive in Gaza and asserting that El-Sayed has longstanding family ties to the Muslim ⁠Brotherhood.
Strategists said homing in on the Muslim Brotherhood also aims to hurt El-Sayed by exploiting economic tensions between Black voters and Michigan’s large Arab-American community.
Asked about Rogers’ strategy, campaign spokesperson Alyssa Brouillet said El-Sayed’s “extremist positions” on issues ranging from prisons to the Muslim Brotherhood were alienating Michiganders.

stories.title: Lahore permits kite-flying from March 12-14 for Basant 2027
summary: The Lahore district administration on Friday allowed kite-flying across the district, except in designated prohibited areas, from March 12 to 14, 2027, as part of Basant celebrations.
The Lahore deputy commissioner issued a formal notification outlining the dates, conditions and safety measures governing the manufacture, sale and use of kites and strings.

Read: Punjab reschedules Lahore Basant to March The purchase, transportation and storage of kite-flying materials would be allowed from February 1, 2027, while their sale would be permitted from February 10 to March 14.

stories.title: PM sets indicative wheat price at Rs4,500 per maund for 2027
summary: The PMO statement added that the prime minister’s decision was aimed at “promoting agriculture sector in the country, protecting farmers’ economic interests and increasing wheat production next year”.

Last month, the Pakistan Kissan Ittehad demanded a Rs5,000 per 40kg support price for wheat, warning that farmers may not sow wheat for the next season if the government delays announcing crop policies.

On Oct 13, PM Shehbaz chaired the first National Agricultural and Food Security Council meeting and reaffirmed that the government wanted farmers to get a fair price for wheat and consumers to have affordable wheat.

stories.title: Govt increases diesel by Rs1.91, keeps petrol unchanged till Oct 26
summary: The federal government on Friday increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.91 per litre while keeping the price of petrol unchanged till October 26.

On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.

Oil prices rose ​on Friday, with Brent crude touching its highest since late April, after Houthi attacks in Saudi ‌Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East, where UAE authorities also reported an oil spill.

stories.title: Brent crude hits more than five-month high on concern over Middle East escalation
summary: Oil prices rose on Friday, with Brent crude touching a more than five-month high, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.
Brent crude futures gained $1.40, or 1.2 per cent, to $114.57 a barrel by 1138 GMT (4:38pm PKT), having earlier reached $115 for the highest level since May 4.
US West Texas Intermediate crude gained $1.48, or 1.5pc, to $100.95.

stories.title: Iran has detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea cables if war resumes, officials say
summary: Tehran has drawn up detailed plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the United States and Israel attack Iran again, two senior Iranian security officials ​told Reuters.

Yadollah ​Javani, the deputy head of political affairs for Iran's Revolutionary Guards (IRGC), said on Wednesday that Iran could target seven major internet cables beneath ⁠the Strait of Hormuz if Iranian infrastructure came under attack.

Washington's Gulf allies have invested heavily in such infrastructure and they "should hold Washington, not Tehran, responsible for any damage to undersea cables," the second Iranian ‌security official ⁠said.

stories.title: Auto illusion
summary: PAKISTAN’S draft auto policy 2026-31 is ambitious in its targets and directionless in its strategy.
The proposed policy aims to generate $6bn in exports over five years, while reducing import tariffs and promoting ‘new’ energy vehicles.
By granting PHEVs a substantial tax advantage, the government is effectively treating vehicles that continue to largely depend on petrol as a preferred route to electrification.

stories.title: At least 12 killed, 22 injured in road accident near Zero Point in Balochistan’s Uthal
summary: KHUZDAR: At least 12 passengers were killed and around two dozen injured when a minibus and a passenger coach collided head-on near Zero Point in Uthal on the Quetta-Karachi Highway in Balochistan on Friday, police said.

A similar accident occurred last month when two people were killed and 15 others injured in a head-on collision between a passenger coach and an LPG bowser near Balochistan’s Kharkhera Customs on the main National Highway in Winder.
In January, four people were killed and several others injured in a road accident near Wadh in Khuzdar district on the Quetta-Karachi National Highway.

stories.title: 10 India-sponsored terrorists killed as bid to undermine state's writ in Gwadar foiled: ISPR
summary: Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Friday that 10 India-sponsored terrorists were killed in separate engagements as security forces thwarted their attempts to “undermine the writ of the state” in Balochistan’s Gwadar district.
The ISPR statement comes a day after security sources said that security forces killed three terrorists and foiled an attack on an unoccupied construction company camp in Gwadar.
Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years, prompting security forces to intensify counter-terrorism operations.
